citations.short: Procedures not  in writing, fully followed
citations.long: The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing.
Employees are not given training in the particular operations they perform as part of their function.

citations.short: Buildings of Suitable Size, Construction, Location
citations.long: Buildings used in the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of a drug product do not have the suitable construction to facilitate cleaning, maintenance, and proper operations.

citations.short: Product flow through building is inadequate
citations.long: The flow of components, drug product containers, closures, labeling, in-process materials, and drug products though the building is not designed to prevent contamination.

citations.short: Defined areas of adequate size for operations
citations.long: The separate or defined areas and control systems necessary to prevent contamination or mix-ups are deficient.
Equipment used in the manufacture, processing, packing or holding of drug products is not of appropriate design, of adequate size, and suitably located to facilitate operations for its intended use.
Equipment and utensils are not cleaned at appropriate intervals to prevent contamination that would alter the safety, identity, strength, quality or purity of the drug product.
Representative samples are not taken of each shipment of each lot of components, drug product containers, and closures for testing or examination.

Reports of analysis from component suppliers are accepted in lieu of testing each component for conformity with all appropriate written specifications, without establishing the reliability of the supplier's analyses through appropriate validation of the supplier's test results at appropriate intervals.

citations.short: Control procedures to monitor and validate performance
citations.long: Control procedures are not established which monitor the output and validate the performance of those manufacturing processes that may be responsible for causing variability in the characteristics of in-process material and the drug product.
Established laboratory control mechanisms are not followed and documented at the time of performance.
Test procedures relative to appropriate laboratory testing for pyrogens are not followed.
There is a failure to thoroughly review any unexplained discrepancy whether or not the batch has been already distributed.

An NDA-Field Alert Report was not submitted within three working days of receipt of information concerning a failure of one or more distributed batches of a drug to meet the specifications established for it in the application.
